title: Sep 23 Results + Sep 24 Preview: A Perfectly Balanced Universe
summary: Sep 23 went 8-8—here's what happened and why tomorrow's Pirates pick has my attention

content.value:
## Here's the Thing About Going .500

September 23rd gave us the most perfectly balanced day possible: 8 wins, 8 losses, a clean 50% split. It's the kind of day that makes you lean back in your chair and think about the beautiful chaos of baseball. Some picks felt like locks that crumbled. Others were coin flips that landed our way. That's the game.

## The Wins That Worked

The Yankees took care of business against the Rays at 60% confidence—exactly the kind of home favorite that delivers. The Orioles swept both picks in their doubleheader against the Jays, and the Braves did what the Braves do, handling the Reds with authority. The White Sox upset pick against the Guardians at 60%? That one felt good.

## The Misses That Stung

The Tigers couldn't hold up our 60% confidence. The Pirates, Cardinals, and Phillies all went the other direction despite decent probabilities. And the White Sox—after winning one pick—couldn't duplicate it against the Royals at 59%. That's baseball in late September. Fatigue, lineup changes, and pure randomness all collide.

## Tomorrow's Story: Pirates vs Cardinals, Round Two

Here's where it gets interesting. We're going back to the same matchup that didn't work yesterday—Cardinals at Pirates. But tomorrow brings a completely different narrative. Paul Skenes takes the mound for Pittsburgh, and if you know anything about September baseball, you know that changes everything.

Kyle Leahy gets the ball for St. Louis, and while he's capable, this is about the mismatch. Skenes has that October-preview energy, the kind of pitcher who can single-handedly shift a series. At 51% confidence, this isn't a screaming certainty—it's a measured read on pitching dominance.

content.title: ⭐ Sep 24 Top Pick
content.sub: 51% win probability · Paul Skenes vs Kyle Leahy

content.value:
## The Human Angle

What I love about this pick is the redemption narrative. Yesterday, the Pirates couldn't deliver at 54%. Tomorrow, they get a slightly lower probability but a significantly better story. Skenes on the mound in late September, protecting a playoff push or building momentum for next year—whatever the stakes, he's the kind of arm you want to bet on.

The Cardinals are fighting their own battles, but facing a pitcher like Skenes this late in the season is a brutal assignment. Sometimes the model captures what our eyes see: pure talent tipping the scales.

Let's see if September 24th breaks us away from that .500 equilibrium. My money—and my heart—is on the kid in Pittsburgh.
